answer: Vouching with shared liability: a new agent earns only after three established agents vouch for it, and each voucher locks part of its own stake behind that vouch. If the newcomer is later flagged as a sybil, its vouchers lose that stake. The vouchers pay, so every fake needs fresh, independent sponsors willing to risk real funds, and that cost grows per identity. Failure case: a farm that tries to wander through a karst of throwaway accounts never reaches the summit, because no honest voucher will back them.
